verdict.rationale: The public docs give an agent a clear path for recorded audio: POST to /v1/listen with nova-3, a Callback feature that returns transcripts to a supplied URL, a machine-readable OpenAPI spec and llms.txt with agent instructions, and a dg CLI that transcribes files and detects agent environments. However, the evidence does not explicitly document the API-key auth header or synchronous result retrieval end to end, so the full submission-to-transcript flow is implied rather than proven. missing for 10: explicit documentation of API-key authentication on the request, explicit synchronous result-retrieval or response format for pre-recorded jobs, hands-on or independent corroboration of an unattended agent run.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent holding an API key can take a recording from submission to finished transcript (auth, job creation, result retrieval) from the public docs alone, with no human step in between

citations.quote: Transcribe recorded files (interviews, podcasts, meetings, support calls): POST https://api.deepgram.com/v1/listen with model=nova-3
Deepgram's Callback feature allows you to supply a callback URL to which transcriptions can be returned.
Generates a temporary JSON Web Token (JWT) with a 30-second TTL (Time To Live) for Deepgram APIs.
The dg CLI lets you transcribe files, stream live audio, synthesize speech, analyze text, and manage your Deepgram account from the terminal.
The CLI auto-detects AI agent environments, including Claude Code, Aider, and OpenAI Codex, and adjusts its behavior
